question.text: A For-Profit Social Enterprise (FPE) can be registered under the Companies Act 2013 in which of the following forms?

answer.text: Only as a Private Limited Company with mandatory SEBI FPE licence
As a Sole Proprietorship, Limited Liability Partnership, Partnership, Private Limited or Public Limited company
Only as a Producer Company under Part IX-A of the Companies Act 1956

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 1.3.2, FPEs can be registered as Sole Proprietorship, LLP, Partnership, Private Limited or Public Limited company — provided the entity meets the 67% primacy-of-social-intent test. They are NOT restricted to Section 8. The Trap: Option A restricts to Section 8 — that is the non-profit route. Option B fabricates an 'FPE licence'. Option D restricts to Producer Company, which is only one sub-form. Cross-Exam Context: Cross-links to Ch 2 (SSE Introduction) and Ch 3 (Registration). SIAs should confirm legal form via MCA-21 before mapping 67% tests. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Different legal forms trigger different audit-trail requirements: a Sole Proprietorship has no separate legal personality (so personal and SE finances may be commingled), while a PLC has stricter governance. Adjust your SAS-100 materiality based on legal form.
